top_improvements: 1. Systematically capture all key history items—including polyuria, polydipsia, weight change, smoking/alcohol, diet, exercise, medication details, family history, and psychosocial concerns—using a structured ROS template.

2. Perform the full set of required physical exams (orthostatic BP, mucous inspection, acanthosis nigricans, fundoscopy, foot neuro exam, monofilament, vibration, DTR, genital exam) and record findings in the chart.
3. Provide a definitive diagnosis statement with disease type and certainty level, and link it explicitly to collected data.

4. Create a clear, actionable order set for initial investigations (fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipid panel, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis, TSH, fundoscopic referral, vaginal swab) and document it in the plan section.
5. Use active learning techniques (e.g., teach–back, summarization) to confirm patient understanding and reduce repetitive statements; focus on concise, patient‑centered communication.
